messages.author: e5c9e77ddb11312c
messages.subject: dplyr group by symmetrical matrices
parts:
I'm trying to figure out how to write flexible code for subsetting a distance matrix for downstream analysis and plotting.


little.dist <-  structure(list(B.R18 = c(NA, 0.276303, 0.125914, 0.129066, 0.838587, 0.834047), C.C11 = c(NA, NA, 0.339285, 0.314995, 0.770283, 0.759652 ), C.C16 = c(NA, NA, NA, 0.126101, 0.821724, 0.81644), C.C19 = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, 0.799399, 0.793513), HC1 = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, 0.336314), HC5 = c(NA_real_, NA_real_, NA_real_, NA_real_, NA_real_, NA_real_)), .Names = c("B.R18", "C.C11", "C.C16", "C.C19", "HC1", "HC5"), row.names = c("B.R18", "C.C11", "C.C16", "C.C19", "HC1", "HC5"), class = "data.frame")

little.group <- structure(list(invsimpson_hci = c(2.796736, 5.018727, 2.845905, 3.165948, 18.308151, 22.14335), Study = structure(c(2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 4L, 4L), .Label = c("10wkHFD", "4wkSM", "BserumPLT", "Plgutmicrobiota" ), class = "factor"), Diet = structure(c(3L, 12L, 12L, 12L, 4L, 4L), .Label = c("Bserum", "CTL", "ESM", "HFC", "HFDC", "HFE", "HFM", "LFC", "LFDC", "LFE", "LFM", "MSM"), class = "factor"), withinstudyordinance = c(3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 4L, 4L), Crossstudyordinance = c(0L, 5L, 5L, 5L, 5L, 5L)), .Names = c("invsimpson_hci", "Study", "Diet", "withinstudyordinance", "Crossstudyordinance"), class = "data.frame", row.names =  c("B.R18", "C.C11", "C.C16", "C.C19", "HC1", "HC5"))


My previous clunky way to do this was to create a dist and group object for each Study:

wk4.dist <- little.dist[little.group$Study=="4wkSM",little.group$Study=="4wkSM"]
wk4.group <- little.group[little.group$Study=="4wkSM",little.group$Study=="4wkSM"]

then run downstream analyses. This seems like it'd be a good application for dplyr but I can't figure out how to subset the dist while keeping it square for downstream analyses (I'll be using as.dist on the dataframes)

thanks

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: dplyr group by symmetrical matrices
parts:
I don't know if others will agree but I'm really not sure what you want to do beyond a filter() step. 

# bind datasets together
df1 <- cbind(little.group, little.dist)

wk4.dist2 <- 
filter(df1, Study == "4wkSM") %>% #filter datsets
select_(., .dots = list(names(little.dist))) # you can then use select() to select only columns from your original dist

Do you have a more complete dataset? I suspect you should use your grouping variable and then you could run as.dist and do some further processing, but it's not clear what you need at the end. 
B
